material_definitions: LiTi2(PO4)3 had poor ionic conductivity and showed high porosity in the sintered pellets.
The partial substitution of the P5+ site with Si4+ or of the Ti4+ site with M3+ in the LiTi2(PO4)3 system was very effective for the enhancement of the conductivity.
Mixing binders such as Li2O or Li4P2O7 with LiTi2(PO4)3 is also successful in obtaining a high conductivity lithium ionic conductor.
The conductivity enhancement by the substitution or the binder addition resulted mainly from the densification of the sintered pellets.
The increase of the lithium content at the grain boundaries is also effective in the conductivity enhancement.
Mixed phosphates of the type A(I)B(IV)2(PO4)3, where A can be Li, Na, or K and B can be Ge, Ti, Hf, or Zr, feature a three-dimensional network of BO6 octahedra and PO4 tetrahedra.
The LiTi2(PO4)3-based solid electrolytes prepared in this study exhibit a rhombohedral crystal structure with the R-3c space group.
Samples in the Li1+xTi2SixP3-xO12 system were synthesized and sintered at 1473 K for 2 hours, resulting in significantly enhanced conductivity and decreased porosity at x = 0.3.

The Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3 systems were explored by substituting Ti4+ with various trivalent cations (Al, Cr, Ga, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, Y, La), where single-phase rhombohedral structures are generally formed for smaller ions.
Sintering properties and density were improved by adding binders like Li2CO3 or (NH4)2HPO4, which decompose into a glassy second phase at the grain boundaries during heat treatment.
